correctness.rationale: The finite domain is specified by 25 board squares and the bishop-attack predicate. The reproducer enumerates every face, all 12 actual tetrahedron/free-triangle elementary collapses, BFS tree generators, and all 58 valid one-generator attaching-word substitutions. The residual two-cell attaching words freely reduce to the identity: factors are a circle plus five two-spheres, and two circles plus three two-spheres. Their join gives exactly (2,13,15) spheres in dimensions (3,4,5). Exact integer Smith forms give ranks (12,33,8) and (11,25,4), corroborating torsion-freeness. No unsupported extension to other boards is asserted.

evidence: Ziegler Theorem 0.1 gives a sufficient diamond shape condition for pure vertex decomposability; his broader theorem concerns skeleton shellability, not the two exact nonpure homotopy types.

Clark–Zeckner restrict their stated class to triangular boards with positive multiplicity at every row length; both identified bishop diagonal boards omit lengths. Their theorem does not yield the two reported mixed dimensions.
Shareshian–Wachs analyze complete matching and chessboard complexes and selected noncomplete boards rather than these bishop diagonal boards.

evidence: A bishop attack graph is the line graph of diagonal-incidence bipartite graphs, so its independence complex is the join of two matching complexes. Searches for this equivalent matching/Ferrers formulation returned different graphs and different board topologies.

value.rationale: The bishop placement complex is a canonical configuration space with a directly motivated integral homotopy question. Its two diagonal-color matching complexes are nonpure and contain nonzero homotopy in adjacent dimensions, producing a natural, fully classified three-dimensional range of reduced homology on the five-by-five board. The explicit attaching-word reductions identify information (the full wedge homotopy type) not determined by numerical placement counts or general lower connectivity estimates. This fixed natural instance is a self-contained nontrivial classification; no unsupported downstream significance is claimed.
